payload.rationale: Observed facts: as of 2026-09-19, the official Dune: Part Three site still advertises a December 18, 2026 North American release, December 16 international, and early-access screenings December 14–15, with Warner Bros./Legendary and Villeneuve attached. The question asks whether the release slips past December 18, 2026, with roughly three months remaining. Background knowledge: Dune: Part Three (Dune Messiah) completed principal photography in 2025 and has held its December 2026 date for a long time as a flagship tentpole with IMAX commitments; Warner Bros. moved its date earlier in the past, not later. Major studio tentpoles that are still officially dated within ~90 days of release, with early screenings scheduled and marketing underway, are delayed only rarely; late-stage delays typically require extraordinary events (strikes, disasters, health emergencies, or catastrophic VFX shortfalls). None is indicated in the supplied evidence. Too high: the historical base rate for this stage is very low (likely 1–3%), and the film's IMAX and holiday-slot commitments make a move extremely costly, so 4% may overstate risk. Too low: post-production on a VFX-heavy Villeneuve film is demanding, placeholder text on the official site hints the marketing rollout is not fully mature, and unforeseen industry disruptions or a strategic shift by Warner Bros. (e.g., corporate changes) could still force a slip; also, ambiguity over how a one-day move or staggered releases would be adjudicated adds small tail risk. I set the probability near the low end but above the pure base rate to reflect residual uncertainty.
limitations: No information on actual post-production status, VFX completion, or internal studio scheduling.
No fitted historical base rate for tentpole delays at ~90 days out; estimate relies on general judgment.
Single-source evidence packet (official site) retrieved at cutoff; cannot detect trade reporting of possible date changes.
Resolution adjudication details (e.g., partial-territory moves) not fully specified in supplied rules.
